title: Chemical Bonding I (Ionic & Covalent) - Chemistry - Polarity
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which general trend for electronegativity is correct?
options: Increases down a group, decreases across a period.
Decreases down a group, increases across a period.
Increases down a group, increases across a period.
Decreases down a group, decreases across a period.
questions.explain: Electronegativity increases towards Fluorine (top right). It increases left-to-right across a period and decreases top-to-bottom down a group.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A dipole moment ($\mu$) is created when:
options: There is a separation of positive and negative charge.
A molecule has an even number of electrons.
questions.explain: A dipole moment is a vector quantity that measures the separation of positive and negative electrical charges within a system (e.g., a polar bond).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following bonds is the most polar?
questions.explain: Polarity depends on the electronegativity difference. Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so the difference in H-F is the largest among the options.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is Carbon Dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) nonpolar despite containing polar C=O bonds?
options: The bonds are not actually polar.
The molecule is linear, and the bond dipoles cancel each other out.
The molecule is bent, but the dipoles are weak.
questions.explain: $\text{CO}_2$ is a linear molecule. The two C=O bond dipoles are equal in magnitude but point in opposite directions, canceling to a net dipole of zero.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following molecules is polar?
questions.explain: $\text{NH}_3$ (Trigonal Pyramidal) is asymmetric due to the lone pair on Nitrogen. The bond dipoles do not cancel, resulting in a net dipole moment. The others are symmetric and nonpolar.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The dipole moment ($\mu$) is calculated as $\mu = Q \times r$. If the charge separation increases while the bond length remains constant, what happens to the dipole moment?
questions.explain: Since dipole moment is directly proportional to charge magnitude ($Q​$), increasing $Q​$ increases $\mu$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Compare the isomers of dichloroethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_2$). Which isomer has a net dipole moment of zero?
questions.explain: In trans-1,2-dichloroethene, the two polar C-Cl bonds are on opposite sides of the double bond (180 degrees apart notionally in vector terms relative to the center), canceling each other out perfectly.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Based on the principle 'Like dissolves like', which solvent would be best for dissolving a nonpolar substance like grease ($\text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{38}$)?
questions.explain: Grease is nonpolar. Hexane is a nonpolar solvent. Water, Ammonia, and Ethanol are polar solvents. Nonpolar solutes dissolve best in nonpolar solvents.
questions.subject: Chemistry
